subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce loopback constraint for auth mode none

question: Should `gateway.auth.mode="none"` be enforced as loopback-only at every request-time Gateway auth boundary, including WebSocket, or should this PR be narrowed to a specific HTTP/proxy gap already covered by adjacent work?
rationale: The patch changes a security boundary and can break existing explicit no-auth private-ingress or reverse-proxy setups, while current startup validation already blocks the stated non-loopback bind case.

options.title: Narrow and prove request-time loopback guard
options.body: Keep the fail-closed direction, but add focused HTTP and WebSocket tests plus real gateway/proxy proof and clarify the comment against the existing startup guard.

options.title: Route through adjacent PRs
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102881 for browser Origin hardening and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98022 for managed install safety instead of a broad auth helper guard.

options.title: Accept broad fail-closed behavior
options.body: Land the guard as a deliberate compatibility break after documenting that all request-object none-mode traffic must be direct loopback.

recommendation.title: Narrow and prove request-time loopback guard
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed direction, but add focused HTTP and WebSocket tests plus real gateway/proxy proof and clarify the comment against the existing startup guard.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on Gateway auth/security-boundary policy and no-auth exposure fixes.
